correctness.rationale: For each x at source level i, the principal-upset identity reduces HP+BP exactly to U_i union {f(x)} = up f(x), with one shared strict-upper-source image U_i. For a surjective map, every such U_i must be a completed target-level suffix; a proper partial target-level frontier cannot be completed from any lower source layer. Eligible next images are only the new level and possibly its previous singleton frontier, yielding disjoint Stirling-weight stay/advance choices. The induction covers all h,k and all positive level sizes. The labelled thick-target product follows by forbidding all stays. A separate explicit HP/BP direct enumerator agrees with the transfer on 449 small shape pairs and further thick-target cases.

value.rationale: Surjective p-morphism existence is a motivated NP problem for finite intuitionistic Kripke frames. The theorem supplies a complete exact count for every source/target weak-order profile using \(O(hk)\) transfer states, including many non-tree cases not covered by the primary tree algorithm. The all-nonsingleton target rigidity and singleton threshold give structural information about which height collapses can occur, and meaningful exact enumeration not implied by mere map counting.
